title: Application security exposes common developer errors and attack #appsec #securityflaws #devmistakes
description:
Common real-world application security mistakes include trusting the front-end, broken access control, business logic abuse, over-reliance on external APIs, and server-side request forgery (SSRF). Developers often assume that hiding UI elements or relying on client-side checks is sufficient, but attackers bypass these by targeting back-end systems directly, exposing critical vulnerabilities.

Proper permission validation on the server side is essential to prevent unauthorized actions such as deleting users or changing sensitive data. Security also requires full journey validation to stop business logic abuse, like bypassing payments while still receiving rewards. Additionally, validating tokens and responses from external APIs is crucial, as these services can fail or be compromised.

SSRF attacks exploit servers fetching URLs based on user input, enabling attackers to access internal systems undetected. Understanding and mitigating these errors is vital for enhancing application security, protecting user data, and maintaining trust in digital services.
